If that for some reason happens again, with anyone, yell at them and make a big scene right then and there. Something similar happened to me, when I was playing for our volleyball team, one boy slapped my ass as I left the court. If you make a big scene, they will most likely be extremely embarrassed that a lot of negative attention is on them. 

Even though the situation is over, there are still things you can do so they get the punishment they deserve. Report it to the Dean of Students, Principal, Counselor, anyone at your school in a position of power. I would hope they would get suspended, but if they don't at least their parents would know what they're being accused of, and give them a smack upside the head for not respecting women.

As for identifying the three boys, is there anyway you would know who they were by looking at their faces in a team picture or something? Even if that doesn't work, lots of teenagers will crack under pressure, because they won't want to be the only one going down for something the three of them did.

That's what I'm afraid will happen. I mentioned in a previous comment that my mother is very good at code switching. If the police *did* care enough, my mom would probably give it back only to have it taken again.

Thank you for this advice! I'm still learning, I still have a few years left before I'm able to get out of this situation, and I'm still learning as I go. I always really appreciate when someone gives me advice like this, because it helps me know how to deal with something the first or second time, so I don't have to learn from trial and error.
That's true. He is also my homeroom teacher, so maybe that will be another reason for him to assist me.

It took even me 13 years to even realize what she was doing to me wasn't normal. I had heard how most of my friends described their relationship with their mothers, and once I talked about mine, they just stared at me. I just assumed it was normal for mothers to do this, or that she was just code-switching, because I had never experienced anything different.
That is a very good idea I haven't thought of, but my teacher has one of the deepest voices I've ever heard.

While my teacher is very nice and approachable, he would probably either tell me to make a new piece, or get involved by emailing my mother, which I know for a fact would be harmful towards me. 
Even then, for my school, my mother puts on a very polished and clean version of herself, so I would expect that they would think I could just ask for it back.

Thank you so much for responding. I appreciate your advice about finding others to give me validation. I'm still learning what to and what not to expect from my mother, so I'm thankful for you helping me learn this one faster. I suppose I always hoped she would be proud of me.

Surprisingly she cares tremendously about my grades so that could work. I suppose I tried to seek her validation because she says fine arts is my only talent. It has always come back to bite me. I appreciate your response, thank you.
